intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a budget train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport or train station — look for a Migros or Coop grab-and-go sandwich or wrap (CHF 5–8) to keep costs low during transit.

day_by_day.notes: From Zurich HB, take the train to Chur, then connect to the Rhaetian Railway toward Tirano — alight at Poschiavo station. Journey takes approximately 4–5 hours. Book tickets in advance on SBB.ch for best prices. The B&B is a short walk or taxi ride from Poschiavo station. Keep luggage light for easy train travel.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a leisurely morning walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo. Explore the Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate architecture, and visit the Reformed Church of San Vittore. This is a free self-guided walking tour that gives you a feel for the unique Swiss-Italian culture of the Valposchiavo valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a scenic alpine lake just a short walk from the village center. Walk along the lakeside path enjoying stunning winter mountain views. If the lake is partially frozen, it makes for incredible photography. Explore the surrounding snowy meadows and take in the crisp mountain air — a perfect free afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center for a relaxed evening. Browse the small local shops and pick up some budget-friendly Swiss chocolate or local Valposchiavo products as souvenirs. Enjoy a warm drink at a local café before heading back to the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pick up supplies at the local Coop or Migros supermarket in Poschiavo for a self-made picnic lunch by the lake — bread, cheese, salami, and fruit for around CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a local budget-friendly restaurant offering traditional Graubünden dishes like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or polenta with cheese. Expect CHF 18–25 for a main course.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from jet lag and travel fatigue. Poschiavo sits at 1,014m elevation — take it easy to acclimatize before more strenuous activities. Wear warm layers as February temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Bernina Express train from Poschiavo up toward the Bernina Pass (2,253m) — one of the highest railway crossings in the Alps and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Ride up to Ospizio Bernina station and step out into a breathtaking high-alpine winter wonderland. The journey itself is spectacular with viaducts, glaciers, and snow-covered peaks. A short segment ticket costs approximately CHF 10–15.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Ospizio Bernina, enjoy free snowshoeing or winter hiking on the marked trails around Lago Bianco (White Lake), which is typically frozen solid in February. The frozen lake surrounded by glaciers and peaks is one of the most dramatic winter landscapes in Switzerland. Bring your own snacks and hot drinks in a thermos to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo in the late afternoon. Warm up at the B&B with a hot shower, then head out for a budget dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches from the B&B or supermarket to enjoy at Ospizio Bernina — saves significant money versus buying at mountain restaurants.
meals.dinner: Pizzeria/Trattoria in Poschiavo village — pizza or pasta dishes typically CHF 14–20. Look for the daily special (piatto del giorno) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Dress in full winter gear for the Bernina Pass — temperatures at 2,253m can be -15°C to -20°C with wind chill in February. Wear waterproof boots, thermal layers, hat, gloves, and goggles. The train ride is approximately 30 minutes from Poschiavo. Check SBB.ch for timetables. Snowshoes can sometimes be rented in Poschiavo village for CHF 15–20/day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Diavolezza ski area, accessible from Diavolezza station on the Bernina railway line (one stop above Ospizio Bernina). Diavolezza is one of the most spectacular ski resorts in the Alps, offering stunning views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü. Purchase a half-day ski pass (approximately CHF 45–55) for the morning session. Rent ski equipment at the resort base (CHF 35–45 for skis, boots, and poles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza in the early afternoon to maximize your lift pass value. The resort offers runs for all levels — beginners can stick to the easier blue runs while more experienced skiers can tackle the red and black pistes. The views from the top cable car station at 2,978m are absolutely world-class.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon. Rest tired legs at the B&B, then enjoy a quiet evening in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat a substantial breakfast before a full day of skiing.
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, fruit) in a backpack to avoid expensive mountain restaurant prices. Eat at the base area picnic tables or in the ski lodge common area.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Coop/Migros — pasta with local cheese sauce or risotto. Budget CHF 8–12 for ingredients. Many B&Bs allow use of a shared kitchen.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza day ski pass costs approximately CHF 55–65 for adults. Book equipment rental online in advance for potential discounts. The train from Poschiavo to Diavolezza station takes about 40 minutes. This is the most expensive day of the trip — plan accordingly. Consider a half-day pass (afternoon) if budget is very tight, as it costs around CHF 40–45.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Morteratsch Glacier on foot — take the train to Morteratsch station (between Poschiavo and Pontresina) and follow the well-marked 1.5-hour glacier trail. The trail is free and leads you right up to the glacier snout, with marker posts showing how far the glacier has retreated over the decades. A humbling and spectacular experience in a dramatic mountain setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Pontresina, a charming alpine village and winter sports hub. Explore the village on foot, visit the Santa Maria Church with its medieval frescoes, and browse the local shops. Pontresina also has free cross-country skiing (langlauf) trails — if you have or can rent basic cross-country skis (CHF 20–25), this is a very budget-friendly way to enjoy winter sports.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the B&B, perhaps chatting with other guests about their alpine adventures.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Grab a bratwurst or hot snack from a street food stand or bakery in Pontresina — budget CHF 6–10. Alternatively, pack lunch from the B&B.
meals.dinner: Try the local Graubünden specialty Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) at a local restaurant in Poschiavo. Look for set menus or daily specials around CHF 18–22.

day_by_day.notes: The Morteratsch Glacier trail is approximately 3km each way and relatively flat — suitable for all fitness levels. Wear waterproof boots as the trail can be icy. The train from Poschiavo to Morteratsch station takes about 50 minutes. Pontresina is one stop further. Keep your Swiss Travel Pass or day ticket handy for multiple train journeys.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to St. Moritz — the world-famous luxury ski resort, just 30–40 minutes from Poschiavo by Bernina railway. While staying in budget accommodation in Poschiavo, you can enjoy St. Moritz as a day visitor. Start with a free walk around the frozen Lake St. Moritz (Lago di San Murezzan), which in February often hosts the famous White Turf horse racing on ice — check if the event is scheduled (usually held on Sundays in February, CHF 15–20 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore St. Moritz village on foot — window shop the luxury boutiques (free!), visit the Segantini Museum (CHF 10 entry, showcasing alpine landscape paintings), and enjoy the stunning Engadin valley panoramas. For a budget ski option, consider the Corviglia ski area with a half-day pass (CHF 45–55) — more affordable than a full day and you can ski the famous runs used in World Cup competitions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Celebrate your penultimate evening with a slightly more indulgent dinner at the B&B or a local restaurant — you've earned it after a week of budget-savvy travel!

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch to eat by Lake St. Moritz — St. Moritz restaurants are very expensive (CHF 30–50+ for a meal). A packed lunch saves CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — try a traditional Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and Rösti at a local Poschiavo restaurant. Budget CHF 22–28 for a two-course meal.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive resorts, but visiting as a day tripper from budget accommodation in Poschiavo is a smart way to experience it without the luxury price tag. The Bernina Express train between Poschiavo and St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage journey in itself. Saturday may be busier on the slopes — arrive early for shorter lift queues.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last sunrise walk around Poschiavo village and the lake. Take photos of the snow-capped peaks glowing in the morning light. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B. If time allows before departure, visit the local Sunday market in Poschiavo for fresh local produce, cheeses, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your journey home. Take the Bernina Express train from Poschiavo toward Chur or Tirano (depending on your return flight direction), connecting onward to Zurich or Milan. The scenic train journey is the perfect final memory of your Swiss Alps adventure. Use travel time to review photos and plan your next trip!
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Zurich or Milan airport. If you have a long layover, Zurich airport has excellent free viewing areas to watch planes and enjoy final Swiss views.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy a final hearty Swiss breakfast.
meals.lunch: Grab a final Swiss treat at a train station Coop or Migros — try a Gipfeli (Swiss croissant) and coffee for CHF 4–6, or a sandwich for CHF 7–9.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or pack Swiss chocolate and snacks purchased earlier in the week for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Swiss B&Bs is 10:00–11:00. Store luggage at Poschiavo station if needed while you enjoy your final morning. Book return train tickets in advance on SBB.ch. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate, local Valposchiavo wine, or Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart) as affordable, authentic souvenirs. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): CHF 600–800 per person, including accommodation, transport, one ski day, food, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Check in, unpack, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at the airport before boarding or upon arrival if the B&B has a welcome tray. Budget ~CHF 15–20.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your transfer from the nearest airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa) to Poschiavo in advance. The drive from Zurich is approximately 2.5–3 hours; from Milan Malpensa approximately 2 hours. Consider a private shuttle or rental car. Confirm late check-in with the B&B ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast and take a gentle orientation walk around Poschiavo village. Explore the charming Piazza Comunale, the historic Spanish Quarter, and the frozen Lake Poschiavo nearby. This easy start helps you acclimatize to the Alpine altitude and crisp mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take the scenic Bernina Express train (approx. 1.5 hours) toward St. Moritz / Pontresina area. Rent ski equipment at a local ski shop in Pontresina or Diavolezza and enjoy an introductory afternoon ski session at Diavolezza-Lagalb ski area — a stunning glacier ski resort with breathtaking Bernina massif views, suitable for all skill levels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Stroll the village and warm up at a local café with a hot chocolate or Glühwein (mulled wine).

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at the Berninapass Panorama — included with stay. Expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Diavolezza ski area — try a hearty Rösti (Swiss potato cake) or a bowl of Minestrone soup. Budget ~CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a cozy local restaurant serving Graubünden regional specialties like Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and Capuns. Budget ~CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza is approximately 30–40 minutes by car or Bernina Express train from Poschiavo. Purchase a day ski pass at the resort (~CHF 60–70). Ski rental is available at the base. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. Check snow and weather conditions the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour. Depart early from Poschiavo by train via the Bernina Express to Interlaken (approximately 3.5–4 hours with connections). Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, visit the Ice Palace, and enjoy panoramic views of the Bernese Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, walk on the glacier (weather permitting), and browse the Top of Europe exhibition. Begin the descent back toward Interlaken in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward Poschiavo. Due to the long travel day, arrive back at the B&B by 21:00–22:00. Relax and prepare for the next day's skiing.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant or Self-Service Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — enjoy a warm meal with glacier views. Budget ~CHF 25–40. Note: prices are elevated at altitude.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a local Poschiavo café or pick up provisions from a Migros or Coop supermarket for a simple in-room meal. Budget ~CHF 15–25.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — book Jungfraujoch train tickets in advance online (Swiss Travel Pass may offer discounts). Round-trip train ticket to Jungfraujoch costs approximately CHF 145–200 per person (with Swiss Travel Pass discounts available). Dress in very warm layers — temperatures at 3,454m can be -15°C or colder. Altitude sickness is possible; stay hydrated and ascend slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive approximately 2.5 hours northwest to Zermatt (park at Täsch and take the shuttle train — no private cars allowed in Zermatt). Begin the Zermatt Ski Safari experience — explore the legendary slopes with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Start with the Sunnegga Paradise area for stunning Matterhorn views and well-groomed intermediate runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari — progress to the Gornergrat or Klein Matterhorn sectors. Enjoy the variety of blue and red runs, and take the cable car to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m for Europe's highest ski terrain. Ski down through the Italian border to Cervinia if conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Zermatt village — enjoy a drink at one of the lively bars along the Bahnhofstrasse. Attend the Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Zermatt — warm up with traditional Swiss cheese fondue (Gruyère and Emmental blend) paired with local white wine.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast — early start recommended for the drive to Täsch.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant on the slopes — try the Chez Vrony restaurant on the Findeln piste, famous for its stunning Matterhorn views and excellent food. Budget ~CHF 30–45.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening — traditional cheese fondue dinner at Restaurant du Pont or Walliserkanne in Zermatt. Budget ~CHF 45–65 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Park at Täsch parking garage (~CHF 15/day) and take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn shuttle to Zermatt (5 minutes, ~CHF 10 return). Zermatt ski day pass costs approximately CHF 85–95. Book the fondue dinner in advance as popular restaurants fill up quickly. Consider staying overnight in Zermatt to avoid the long return drive — budget hotels like Hotel Bahnhof cost ~CHF 80–120/night if you prefer to split the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Drive approximately 3 hours northeast to Davos (via the scenic Julier Pass or through Chur). Arrive in Davos — the highest city in Europe at 1,560m — and begin the Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail experience. Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around the Davos valley. Rent cross-country ski equipment at the Davos Nordic Center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic skiing on the Davos Flüela or Sertig valley trails — beautiful forested routes with mountain panoramas. Alternatively, if you prefer downhill, Parsenn ski area (Davos-Klosters) offers excellent intermediate and advanced runs. Take a break at a trailside hut for a warm drink.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Davos Platz town center. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant before the drive back toward Poschiavo (approximately 1.5 hours via the Flüela Pass — check if open in winter — or 2 hours via Chur).

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Schatzalp in Davos — a historic mountain hotel with a panoramic restaurant offering traditional Swiss cuisine. Budget ~CHF 25–35.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Bündnerstube in Davos — serving hearty Graubünden specialties like Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and venison dishes. Budget ~CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski pass and rental in Davos costs approximately CHF 30–40 for a day pass plus ~CHF 25–35 for equipment rental. The Flüela Pass (Route 28) may be closed in winter — check road conditions at viasuisse.ch before departure. Alternative return route via Chur adds ~30 minutes but is more reliable. Davos is a great contrast to the downhill skiing days — the Nordic experience is gentler and highly scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Drive approximately 2 hours west to Verbier (via Martigny). Join the Verbier Freeride Experience — a guided off-piste freeride session in one of the world's top freeride destinations. Meet your certified mountain guide at the Verbier ski school meeting point. The guide will assess group skill levels and choose appropriate off-piste terrain. Explore the legendary Mont-Fort glacier area and the famous Vallon d'Arby couloir (conditions permitting).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the freeride session with your guide — explore hidden powder stashes and steep off-piste descents in the 4 Vallées ski area. The guide ensures safety with avalanche equipment briefing and route selection based on current snowpack conditions. End the session with a celebratory run down to the village.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Verbier — one of Switzerland's most vibrant ski resort nightlife scenes. Enjoy drinks at the iconic Farinet Bar or Pub Mont-Fort. Have dinner in Verbier before the drive back to Poschiavo (approximately 2.5–3 hours).

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast — early start for the drive to Verbier.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cabane du Mont-Fort (3,330m) — a legendary mountain hut with stunning views and hearty mountain food. Try the soup and bread or pasta. Budget ~CHF 25–35.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Fer à Cheval restaurant in Verbier — a popular mid-range restaurant with excellent raclette and local Valais wines. Budget ~CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride Experience requires intermediate to advanced skiing ability and prior off-piste experience. Book the guided freeride session in advance through Verbier's ski school (~CHF 120–180 per person for a half-day group session). Avalanche safety equipment (transceiver, probe, shovel) is mandatory — rental available at the ski school. Verbier lift pass costs ~CHF 75–85 for a day. Consider an overnight stay in Verbier to avoid the long return drive — budget accommodation at Chalet Carlsberg or similar runs ~CHF 80–130/night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo — enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast and take a relaxed walk around the village. Visit the local Sunday market if available, or explore the Poschiavo Museum (Museo di Poschiavo) to learn about the valley's unique Romansh and Italian cultural heritage. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a final scenic drive or Bernina Express train ride through the UNESCO World Heritage Bernina landscape — one of the most spectacular mountain railway journeys in the world. Stop at Alp Grüm viewpoint for a last panoramic photo of the Palü glacier and Bernina peaks. Begin your transfer to the departure airport (Zurich ~3 hours, Milan Malpensa ~2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Switzerland. Airport dining or a final Swiss treat — pick up Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Läderach, or local Graubünden varieties) and cheese at the airport duty-free as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Panorama — savor the last mountain views from the dining room.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Alp Grüm — a charming mountain restaurant accessible only by train, perched above the Palü glacier. Try the Pizzoccheri or Polenta with local cheese. Budget ~CHF 25–35.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a light meal en route. Budget ~CHF 20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B is typically 10:00–11:00 — confirm with the host. The Bernina Express to Alp Grüm runs regularly and is included with the Swiss Travel Pass or costs ~CHF 20–30 for a short segment. Allow ample time for the airport transfer — factor in potential winter road delays. Confirm your return flight details and airport terminal in advance. Consider purchasing a Swiss Travel Pass for the week to save on train costs across all excursion days.

meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)

Pack ski gear or arrange rental for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the B&B to recover from travel. Afterward, take a scenic orientation walk through the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the frozen Lake Poschiavo shoreline. Breathe in the crisp Alpine air and acclimatize to the altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a private transfer to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road). Enjoy an introductory afternoon ski session on Livigno's well-groomed pistes — a perfect warm-up for the week. Rent premium ski equipment at a top-tier rental shop in Livigno (e.g., Intersport Livigno or Mottolino Ski Rental). Livigno offers 115km of slopes across all levels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Freshen up at the B&B, then enjoy a premium dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a refined local restaurant offering Graubünden specialties including Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables), venison ragù, and an excellent regional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — freshly baked bread, local honey, mountain butter, cold cuts, regional cheeses, soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the slopes at Livigno — dine at Mottolino's mountain restaurant or Tea del Vidal, enjoying hearty mountain fare such as polenta with cheese, grilled sausages, and mulled wine with panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — multi-course dinner featuring Graubünden regional cuisine. Recommended: Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings), slow-braised venison, and a bottle of local Malanser Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Livigno is technically in Italy but is easily accessible from Poschiavo and offers duty-free shopping — a bonus for luxury goods. Confirm ski rental reservations in advance. Check Bernina Pass road conditions as it can be closed in heavy snowfall; have a backup route via Tirano if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the B&B, then depart for a full-day Zermatt Ski Safari experience. Take a private luxury transfer or drive to Zermatt (approximately 2.5–3 hours via St. Moritz and the Furka Pass area, or arrange a scenic rail journey on the Glacier Express from St. Moritz to Zermatt for a truly iconic Alpine experience). Arrive in Zermatt — the car-free village beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Meet your private ski guide and begin the Zermatt Ski Safari across 360km of world-class groomed pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari — explore the Klein Matterhorn sector (highest skiing in the Alps at 3,883m), the Rothorn area, and the Sunnegga Paradise zone. Your guide will tailor the route to your skill level and preferences, ensuring access to the finest runs with breathtaking Matterhorn views throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down in Zermatt village. Enjoy a luxurious dinner at Restaurant Zum See — one of Switzerland's most celebrated mountain restaurants, set in a 300-year-old farmhouse in the forest. Reservations are essential. Alternatively, dine at Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope for refined Alpine cuisine with unmatched Matterhorn views. Overnight in Zermatt at a luxury property (e.g., The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace) is strongly recommended to avoid the long return transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Zermatt — dine at Chez Vrony (Findeln) or Blauherd Restaurant, enjoying gourmet mountain cuisine including truffle pasta, Alpine beef tartare, and local Valais wines.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum See, Zermatt — legendary fine dining in a rustic Alpine farmhouse. Seasonal tasting menu featuring Valais lamb, wild mushroom risotto, and an exceptional Swiss wine cellar. Pre-booking mandatory.

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express from St. Moritz to Zermatt is a world-famous scenic rail journey (approx. 7.5 hours) — if time allows, consider taking it one way and arranging a private transfer for the return. Zermatt is car-free; electric taxis are available within the village. Book ski guide and restaurant reservations well in advance. Consider an overnight stay in Zermatt to fully enjoy the evening without a long transfer back.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight in Zermatt: morning ski run on freshly groomed pistes before the crowds arrive — the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise sector is magical at dawn. If returning to Poschiavo: depart Zermatt after breakfast and travel to Verbier (approximately 1.5 hours by private transfer). Arrive in Verbier — the glamorous ski resort beloved by royalty and celebrities — and meet your certified mountain guide for the Verbier Freeride Experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Verbier Freeride Experience — join your expert guide for a guided off-piste freeride session across Verbier's legendary backcountry terrain. Explore the iconic Mont Fort sector (3,330m), the Stairway to Heaven couloir area, and the vast untracked powder fields of the Quatre Vallées. Safety equipment (avalanche transceiver, probe, shovel) provided. This experience is tailored to intermediate-advanced skiers; alternatives available for all levels.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Verbier at the legendary Farinet Bar or Pub Mont Fort. Then enjoy a premium dinner at Restaurant La Grange in Verbier — a sophisticated Alpine restaurant known for its Raclette au feu de bois (wood-fire raclette), Wagyu beef fondue, and curated Swiss wine list. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer or overnight in Verbier.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Zermatt hotel or a Verbier café upon arrival — try Café de la Poste in Verbier for freshly baked croissants, bircher muesli, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch during the freeride experience — Cabane du Mont Fort (3,330m) offers a spectacular high-altitude lunch with panoramic views of the Grand Combin and Mont Blanc massif. Hearty mountain soup, cheese plates, and hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: Restaurant La Grange, Verbier — refined Valais cuisine in a warm, candlelit chalet setting. Signature dishes: wood-fire raclette with cornichons and charcuterie, slow-cooked Hereford beef, and a selection of Swiss artisan cheeses to finish.

day_by_day.notes: Verbier freeride requires a minimum intermediate-advanced ski level. Confirm fitness and skill level with the guide operator when booking. Avalanche safety briefing is included. Verbier is approximately 3.5–4 hours from Poschiavo by private transfer — consider an overnight stay in Verbier (e.g., W Verbier or Chalet d'Adrien) to maximize the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Poschiavo or depart from Verbier/Zermatt area toward the Bernese Oberland. Depart early for the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour. Travel to Grindelwald or Interlaken (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Verbier by private transfer). Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald Terminal or Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. The journey itself is a spectacular engineering marvel through the heart of the Eiger.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jungfraujoch — visit the Ice Palace (carved entirely within the Aletsch Glacier), walk the Sphinx Terrace for 360-degree views of the Alps, and experience the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven exhibition. On a clear day, views extend to the Black Forest in Germany and the Vosges in France. Optional: snowshoe walk on the glacier plateau or a short ski run from the summit (equipment rental available on-site). Descend back to Grindelwald or Interlaken by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Interlaken or travel back toward Poschiavo. Dinner at Restaurant Schuh in Interlaken — a grand historic establishment offering refined Swiss cuisine, live piano music, and an elegant atmosphere. Alternatively, if returning to Poschiavo, stop for dinner at Hotel Croce Federale in Poschiavo for a warm, locally sourced dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation before departure — full Alpine spread or hotel breakfast buffet.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — the highest restaurant in Europe. Enjoy a set lunch menu with panoramic glacier views. Alternatively, the Bollywood Restaurant at Jungfraujoch offers a unique Indian-Swiss fusion experience.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schuh, Interlaken — established in 1818, offering classic Swiss dishes including Bernese Rösti, lake trout, and a legendary dessert selection. Live piano accompaniment in the grand dining room.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in peak winter season. The Good Morning Ticket (early departure) offers a discount and avoids crowds. Dress in very warm layers — temperatures at 3,454m can reach -15°C or below. The journey from Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch takes approximately 45 minutes. Allow a full day for this experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Davos (approximately 1.5 hours from Poschiavo via the scenic Engadin Valley). Arrive in Davos — the highest city in Europe at 1,560m — and begin the Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail experience. Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails across the stunning Davos-Klosters landscape. A certified Nordic guide will lead you through the most scenic routes, including the Flüela Valley trail and the lakeside Davosersee circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic skiing or transition to a snowshoe hike through the pristine Sertig Valley — one of the most beautiful side valleys in Graubünden, accessible from Davos. The valley offers dramatic mountain scenery, frozen waterfalls, and complete Alpine solitude. Visit the historic Walser settlement of Sertig Dörfli. Return to Davos town center by late afternoon for a visit to the Kirchner Museum (dedicated to Expressionist painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, who lived in Davos).
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in the Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening experience — warm up after a day on the Nordic trails with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. In Davos, dine at Restaurant Bündnerstube at the Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère — an iconic establishment offering classic Graubünden fondue, raclette, and Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) in a refined yet cozy Alpine setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure — full Alpine spread with local specialties.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Sertig — a charming mountain restaurant in the Sertig Valley serving homemade soups, Graubünden barley soup, venison goulash, and freshly baked bread. A true hidden gem.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at Restaurant Bündnerstube, Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère, Davos — traditional Graubünden cheese fondue (Vacherin and Gruyère blend), accompanied by crusty bread, cornichons, pearl onions, and a crisp Fendant white wine from Valais. Finish with a Kirsch digestif.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski and snowshoe equipment rental is available in Davos town center. The Davos Nordic trail pass covers all 100km of groomed trails. The Sertig Valley road is accessible by local bus or taxi from Davos Platz. Book the Bündnerstube dinner reservation in advance — it is popular with both locals and visitors. Davos is approximately 1.5 hours from Poschiavo, making it an ideal day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, indulgent breakfast at B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama. Take a slow morning walk along the shores of Lake Poschiavo, soaking in the panoramic views of the surrounding peaks one last time. Visit the local Sunday market in Poschiavo if available — pick up artisan cheeses, local honey, Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), and Graubünden wines as premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional final activity: a scenic drive or private guided tour along the UNESCO World Heritage Bernina Railway route — one of the most spectacular mountain railway journeys in the world, passing through dramatic viaducts, glaciers, and Alpine villages between Poschiavo and St. Moritz. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa afternoon at a luxury wellness facility in St. Moritz (e.g., Badrutt's Palace Hotel Spa or the Kempinski Grand Hotel des Bains) — approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium restaurant in St. Moritz — dine at Restaurant Acla da Fans at Badrutt's Palace Hotel or Matsuhisa St. Moritz (Nobu) for a world-class final evening. Toast to an unforgettable week in the Swiss Alps. Return to Poschiavo for your final night, or arrange an early departure transfer if flying out the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — the full spread: freshly baked Graubünden bread, local mountain cheeses, smoked meats, homemade jams, bircher muesli, fresh fruit, and a celebratory glass of Prosecco.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in St. Moritz — Café Hauser on Via Traunter Plazzas offers legendary homemade cakes, sandwiches, and hot chocolate in a classic Engadin setting. Alternatively, a gourmet picnic assembled from the Poschiavo Sunday market.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Acla da Fans, Badrutt's Palace Hotel, St. Moritz — refined Alpine-Mediterranean cuisine in one of Switzerland's most iconic luxury hotels. Signature dishes: Engadin lamb, black truffle risotto, and a curated selection from one of the finest wine cellars in the Alps. A truly memorable farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express (Poschiavo to St. Moritz) runs year-round and takes approximately 1 hour — book panoramic car seats in advance through Rhaetian Railway (RhB). St. Moritz is 45 minutes from Poschiavo by car or train, making it an ideal base for the final day. If departing by air, Zurich Airport is approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo; Milan Malpensa is approximately 2 hours. Arrange a private luxury transfer for your departure. Confirm all bookings and transfers the evening before.
